\end{figure}

\subsection{Does a real search tool agree with the replay?}
\label{sec:tool}

We ran the \texttt{dspy} 3.0.4 optimiser \texttt{BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch} live with the study's scorer as its language model: $19$ candidate programs (sets of two bootstrapped and two labelled demonstrations, and zero-shot variants), trained and validated on the same $n=60$ items $S$, $24$ draws of $S$, truth the selected program's accuracy on $400$ pool items outside $S$ (Table~\ref{tab:tool}, Appendix~\ref{app:definitions}).
It reports $0.357$ for programs with fresh accuracy $0.291$, a gap of $0.066$ (interval over draws $0.039$--$0.093$; positive in $20$ of $24$ draws); not scoring a program's demonstration items on themselves lowers it to $0.048$, so $0.018$ is leakage. The search-log prediction from the $19\times60$ scores is $0.054$, $0.82$ times the gap.
Random search over $20$ configurations replayed at $n=60$ gives $0.058$. By the rule fixed before the run (the tool's mean inside the replay's pool-bootstrap interval, $0.052$--$0.065$) the result is \emph{not consistent}: the tool's mean is $0.0015$ above the upper end, and inside the corrected interval ($0.049$--$0.067$).
The difference of $0.008$ has a standard error of $0.013$: $24$ draws neither separate the replay from the tool nor show them equal.


\subsection{Beyond the measured matrix}
\label{sec:beyond}

A generative model fitted to the matrix (Section~\ref{sec:method}) predicts the measured gap on held-out items to within the interval of the measurement in $24$ of $24$ split-half checks and in $23$ of $24$ when fitted on $75$ of the $128$ configurations only; it overstates the gap by about $6\%$ ($+0.0035$ on a measured gap of $0.062$).
The measurement interval is $0.039$ wide, so this is a weak test, and it does not tell the three models of dependence between configurations apart.
Extended to $n=800$ and $K=512$, outside the validated support $n\le200$, $K\le128$, the max-t bound covers $96$--$99\%$ and Bonferroni $99$--$100\%$ (Figure~\ref{fig:beyond}).

A repository's URL is `$HT_FORGEJO_URL/<owner>/<repo>.git`, and its wiki's `$HT_FORGEJO_URL/<owner>/<repo>.wiki.git` (pages are Markdown files on its `main`). `$HT_FORGEJO_URL` is the whole base URL (Git signs in for you) and changes from turn to turn: build every URL from it, never reuse an address from an earlier turn. Push and check the remote. Only the owner pushes branches and tags to a repository, and to its wiki, but for the root's `dev`. To propose changes where you read pull requests, base your commit on the target branch and `git push $HT_FORGEJO_URL/world/<role>.git HEAD:refs/for/<branch>/<topic>`. This opens a pull request; the newest commit message gives its title and description, and pushing the same topic updates it. Name the topic in the ref, give no push options, and push nothing else there. `forge` does not open these: read, discuss and review pull requests with `forge` or `forge api`. Copy SHAs from `role_commits` or `git rev-parse`, never from memory or shortened.

- `forge` for issues, pull requests, comments, reviews and releases, already authenticated. It takes the repository from the current directory's `origin`, so outside `/hutian/repo` give it with `-R world/<role>`, `forge api` included. The forms that work here:
  - open an issue: `forge issue create -t <title> -b "$(cat <file>)"`; there is no `--body-file`, and `-a <role>` assigns it;
  - comment on an issue or a pull request: `forge issue comment <number> -b "$(cat <file>)"`; the body is never a positional argument, and only `forge issue comment` (not `forge comment`) prints the reason when the world refuses a comment; `forge issue close <number>` closes, without a comment;
  - read one with its comments: `forge issue view <number> -c`, or `forge pr view <number> -c`; `forge pr diff <number>` shows a pull request's change;
  - review: `forge pr review approve <number> -b <text>`, `forge pr review reject <number> -b <text>`, `forge pr review list <number>`; merge with `forge pr merge <number> -m merge`, or schedule the merge for when Forgejo allows it with `curl -fsS -u "$HT_FORGEJO_USER:$FORGEJO_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"Do":"merge","merge_when_checks_succeed":true}' "$HT_FORGEJO_URL/api/v1/repos/world/<role>/pulls/<number>/merge"` (`forge` cannot send that value);
  - anything else through `forge api <endpoint>`, with `-X <method>` and one `-f key=value` per field (there is no `--input`); `forge api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>/comments` returns a whole thread, unpaginated: filter it with `since`/`before` or locally.
- `apply_patch` may be missing; write small files with `cat > file <<'EOF'` or Python.
- Releases carry files of any size, a web page or a build included: `forge release create --tag <tag> --title <title>` publishes one from your repository, `forge release list -R world/<role>` lists a role's, and `forge api repos/world/<role>/releases/tags/<tag>` gives a release's `id` and each file's `browser_download_url`. Upload with `curl -fT <file> -X POST -u "$HT_FORGEJO_USER:$FORGEJO_TOKEN" "$HT_FORGEJO_URL/api/v1/repos/world/figtab-repo/releases/<id>/assets?name=<name>"` and download with `curl -fLo <file> -u "$HT_FORGEJO_USER:$FORGEJO_TOKEN" <browser_download_url>`: `forge release upload` holds the whole file in memory and `forge release download` does not work here.
